key_insight: SPARC, a transformer-based model of longitudinal health measurements, predicted cancer-related adverse events and generalized across multiple external centers.
clinical_relevance: Risk predictions could help target supportive care, with the study reporting identification of patients most likely to benefit from G-CSF.
method: Pre-trained and fine-tuned on routinely collected, longitudinal health measurements.
Evaluated on held-out, prospective same-center, and external cohorts.
Compared pooled multi-institution with single-institution fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Training used 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients; evaluation included a prospective cohort of 23,126 patients and external cohorts of 26,012, 562,620, and 206,840 patients.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether model-guided care improves patient outcomes; prospective clinical-impact evaluation remains needed.
paper_title: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
